hints.content:
We define function $h$ using a definite integral of function $f$. For every $x$-value, we calculate $h(x)$ by taking the definite integral of $f$ from $-4$ to $x$.

So to calculate $h(\goldD{-2})$ we need to take the definite integral of $f$ from $-4$ to $\goldD{-2}$:

$h(\goldD{-2})=\displaystyle\int_{-4}^{\goldD{-2}}f(t)\,dt$

This represents the net area between the graph of $f(t)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=-4$ to $x=-2$.

We can find $\displaystyle\int_{-4}^{\goldD{-2}}f(t)\,dt$ using geometric area formulas.

![The graph of function f has the region between the segments and the x-axis, between x = negative 4 and x = negative 2, shaded. The segment at the top of the shaded region starts at (negative 4, 8), moves downward to (negative 3, 6), then moves upward to (negative 2, 7).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/69e3b5f376096e68c9a5ae79748f54ca13b872ec)

We have a $2$ by $6$ rectangle, a $1$ by $2$ right triangle, and a right triangle that occupies half a unit square, so in total the area is $13.5$.
